notes.title: Game controls extended in SUPERVERSE Update #18
notes.notes:
The 18th update of SUPERVERSE extends the options to maneuver the spaceship using a game controller and introduces one more way to play the game.

You can now use the D-Pad on a game controller to rotate the spaceship in a clockwise direction by pressing [b]RIGHT on the D-Pad[/b] and to rotate the spaceship in a counterclockwise direction by pressing [b]LEFT on the D-Pad[/b].

The Thruster can now be activated and precisely controlled by pressing the [b]Right Trigger (RT)[/b].

Using D-Pad for rotation and RT for controlling the speed of the spaceship matches the controls you can find in many racing games with top-down view. This also matches the controls you have when playing the game using a keyboard.

We shuffled the default buttons layout and the buttons for activating Primary and Secondary Weapon have been moved to [b]Right Bumper (RB)[/b] and [b]Left Bumper (LB)[/b].

The Shield can be activated by pressing the [b]Left Trigger (LT)[/b].

To summarize, you can now use the game controller to maneuver the spaceship using one of the following combinations:

[list]
[*][b]D-PAD LEFT / RIGHT[/b] for rotation and [b]RT[/b] for thrust
[*][b]LEFT THUMBSTICK[/b] for rotation and thrust combined
[*][b]RIGHT THUMBSTICK[/b] for rotation and [b]RT[/b] for thrust
[/list] 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35079225/8481770abe4554087654b19880b62d68f14d438b.jpg[/img]

notes.title: New Tutorial microverse in Update #14
notes.notes:
The fourteenth update of your favorite SUPERVERSE game is the biggest update released so far. It includes many improvements, changes, performance optimizations, bug fixes, changes in the game balance, and the new game content. 

[h1]Tutorial[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35079225/511b4d041c30fa9b7071a00fbd28db2418a060aa.gif[/img]

A new microverse to start from. The Tutorial will introduce the player to the foundations of the gameplay, the game mechanics and the game controls.

Once successfully completed, the tutorial will be left optional to play.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35079225/5979891a88a6bbefbd22721bf64d7f1a31f0ad22.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35079225/386caf3aa51108a60987f33315db0043e15e7858.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35079225/456f81bfd8a7d4b5abcf7ec551f48493d81c136c.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35079225/d1b7922b0fae074b1f309d6c1cb39539932729c5.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35079225/ae05b697bf06f7ca5de4974f5c04e24096959a08.png[/img]

[h1]More Settings[/h1]
We had to re-think the display Gamma functionality and implement it in a different fashion than it was done in the previous versions of the game. The new version of display Gamma runs well on all the displays. Gamma is now adjustable through [b]Settings > Video > Gamma[/b] option.

New [b]EXPERIMENTAL[/b] setting has been introduced, allowing you to turn the mesh-instancing feature. Mesh-instancing could increase the performance on some slower configurations. Turn it on using [b]Settings > Video > Mesh instancing[/b] option. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35079225/4dc6873f0a6114315b6155de680ec0701139e142.gif[/img]

[b]Settings > Game > Enemy HUD visibility[/b] option allows you to change the way enemy ships are visually marked. The energy scale can be presented permanently over the enemy ship, or it can be presented only when the enemy ship has been hit and is low on energy.

[h1]Integration with Steam[/h1]
This is the first version of the game that links with Steam's library and makes calls to Steamworks API.

Opening Steam layer, by pressing SHIFT + TAB keys or a dedicated button on a game controller, will pause the game. Closing the layer will resume the game automatically.

More Steam related features will be introduced in the forthcoming updates.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35079225/7d629166a0d98d3caa9be4bff40b77d258a9cd47.gif[/img]


[h1]Steam Summer Sale[/h1]
It's already hot. And SUPERVERSE offer during Steam Summer Sale is hot too:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1056170/SUPERVERSE/
[i][b]SUPERVERSE[/b] game is currently available in Early Access for [b]Windows[/b] and [b]Linux[/b] 
(through Steam Play and Proton). [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35079225/3cb0daa3a3494324206cc4fc69ba692f15590ccb.gif[/img]

[h1]Changelog[/h1]

[h2][b]Update #14[/b] | 2020-07-02[/h2]
[list]
[h3]Added[/h3]
[*]The new Tutorial universe introduces the player to the gameplay, game mechanics and controls.
[*]Meteor shower in the background of the main menu on the first run of the game.
[*]The new version of display Gamma runs on all displays, adjustable through [b]Settings > Video > Gamma[/b] option.
[*]New [b]Settings > Game[/b] menu introduced.
[*][b]Settings > Game > Enemy HUD visibility: Constant[/b] option introduced, enabling easier spotting of enemy ships. Turned on by default.
[*]New EXPERIMENTAL [b]Settings > Video > Mesh instancing[/b] option added. Turned Off by default. Mesh instancing could increase the performance on slower configurations.
[*]Initial integration of Steamworks SDK added.
[*]Opening Steam layer (SHIFT + TAB) pauses the game, closing it continues the game.
[*]Sparks have been used for the first time in the new Tutorial universe.
[/list][list]
[h3]Changed[/h3]

[*]Music playback improved in situations during scene changes.

[/list][list]
[h3]Fixed[/h3]

notes.title: Update #12: Stability improvements - Part 2
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35079225/df73cd3e1fd0e85d57a48b8c44f9f417f03435fa.jpg[/img]

May is the month of stability improvements. Update #12 fixes all the remaining issues that could cause the game to be unstable and eventually crash.

A detailed list of technical changes follows:

[h1][Update #12] 2020-05-20[/h1]
[h3]Fixed[/h3]
- Incorrect number of fragments of debris left after NPC Destroyer's destruction
- Turret's debris material inheritance
- Removed ability to configure Gamma, as it seems there is a bug in the underlining 3rd party system which could cause the game to crash on some computers.
- Additional check if the selected monitor is still valid, as it may have been disconnected in the meantime when changing fullscreen/window mode and screen resolution.
- Fixed and removed unnecessary collision detection between some objects
- Fixed trails destruction that could cause a crash on some occasions 
- Dynamic materials management

[h3]Added[/h3]
- Semi-automatic stress testing system


Big thank you for the players who supported us with detailed descriptions of issues and testing on their computers.

In case you own some exotic piece of a game controller that is not yet supported by default, or if they are simply not by your liking, you can always change the mappings using Steam's Controller Configuration.

For a more detailed list of changes please read below:

[b]Added[/b]

[b]Fixed[/b]

Thank you for your support.

notes.title: Update #2: Support for integrated Intel graphics, Mac and Linux
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35079225/ab4c0f1278e1b3c308dbfa5b8ea766fd7a40f566.png[/img]

We are working continually on improving the game experience, fixing bugs and adding new capabilities to the game. Here's what we have prepared for the second update.

[h1]Integrated Intel graphics chip support[/h1]
We have resolved the issue that occurred on laptops without a discrete graphics chip (Nvidia or AMD GPU) but with an integrated Intel graphics. This update will enable most players with such laptops to run the game smoothly and without crashes.

Still, we recommend reducing the screen resolution on these laptops, in order to gain better performance and more fluid gameplay.
 
[h1]Linux support[/h1]
It has been confirmed that SUPERVERSE game can be played on Linux systems using [b]Steam Play[/b] (Proton).

You can contribute to ProtonDB and confirm if the game runs fine on your Linux system too: https://www.protondb.com/app/1056170

[h1]Mac support[/h1]
Although SUPERVERSE game does not support macOS natively, the game could have been played on Macs running Windows operating system using [b]Boot Camp[/b] since day one. 

This update allows the game to be played without any problems using [b]Parallels Desktop 15[/b] emulator as well. We have also managed to start the game in VMWare Fusion, but only partially for now.

[h1]What's coming next[/h1]
In the days ahead, we will publish the road-map of the features and functionalities we plan to introduce in the future. The first among those will be the introduction of local co-op multiplayer mode. 

For more detailed changelog read below:
[h1][Update #2] 2019-11-26[/h1]
[b]Added[/b]
 • The game can now be started on Mac using Parallels Desktop 15 emulator.

[b]Changed[/b]
 • Smoother camera behavior.

[b]Fixed[/b]
 • Fixed the problem where after setting music volume to 0% the music could still be heard.
 • Fixed the problem with memory consumption on PCs featuring integrated Intel GPU; resulting in improved stability and slightly better performance.

notes.title: The first update
notes.notes:
Since releasing the SUPERVERSE game into Early Access, we have been continuously working on improving some of the aspects of the game in order to streamline the experience for the majority of the players.

This is just the first among many steps, many updates yet to be released.

For the detailed overview of what's new read more below:

[h1][Update #1] 2019-11-15 changelog:[/h1]
[b]Added[/b]
- On laptops featuring both integrated and discrete graphics chip the game will automatically try to use a discrete Nvidia or AMD GPU.

[b]Changed[/b]
- Menu navigation has been improved, closing in-game menu and resuming the game as well as returning to previous menus using START / OPTION buttons is now possible.
- Menu and spaceship selection using analog controller has been improved, it is less sensitive now.
- Content changes made in the first universe.
- Game difficulty balance changed.
- Text changes.
